name: Darius
interpretive_note: This "Darius the Mede," who received the kingdom immediately after Belshazzar's fall (Daniel 5:31) and appears in the lions' den account of Daniel 6, is a different king from the Persian king Darius I Hystaspes (reigned 522-486 BC) of Ezra 4-6, Haggai, and Zechariah, who decades later authorized completion of the Jerusalem temple -- see that king's own entry, "Darius" (person_id darius-2). Darius the Mede's precise identity outside the book of Daniel is itself disputed among scholars, with proposals including a governor or general serving under Cyrus (sometimes identified with Gubaru/Ugbaru) or another name or title for Cyrus himself; no independent record settles the question, so this entry describes him only as Scripture presents him.
source_summary: King who governed Babylon after its fall to the Medes and Persians and famously ordered Daniel thrown into a den of lions for continuing to pray to the LORD.
family_friendly_summary: The Bible tells us about a king named Darius who ruled after Babylon fell to the Medes and Persians. Darius liked Daniel and planned to put him in charge of his whole kingdom, but jealous officials tricked Darius into signing a law that said no one could pray to anyone except the king for thirty days. Daniel kept praying to God anyway, just like always, so the officials insisted Darius punish him by throwing him into a den of lions. Darius was very upset, but the law couldn't be changed. All night he worried, and at dawn he ran to the den -- and found Daniel completely safe, because God had sent an angel to shut the lions' mouths. Darius praised God and honored Daniel.
adult_story: This king, known as "Darius the Mede" to distinguish him from the later Persian king Darius I of Ezra and Haggai's day, received the kingdom of Babylon at about sixty-two years old after Belshazzar's fall (Daniel 5:30-31). Darius planned to set Daniel over his whole kingdom because of his extraordinary spirit, provoking jealousy among his other officials (Daniel 6:1-4). Unable to find any fault in Daniel's conduct, they trapped Darius into signing an irrevocable law forbidding prayer to anyone but the king for thirty days, specifically to catch Daniel, who continued praying to the LORD three times a day as always (6:5-10). When Daniel was reported, Darius was "deeply distressed" and worked until sundown trying to save him, but the Medo-Persian law could not be revoked, so Daniel was thrown into the lions' den (6:14-17). Darius spent a sleepless night fasting and hurried to the den at dawn, calling out anxiously -- and found Daniel unharmed, because "my God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths" (6:18-22). Darius had Daniel's accusers thrown to the lions instead and issued a decree that all his subjects should fear the God of Daniel (6:23-27).

devotionals: Darius searched all night for a way to save Daniel, but only God could shut the lions' mouths and save him. Only Jesus can save us too.
After seeing Daniel spared, Darius commanded his kingdom to fear the God who rescues and delivers. May that same God lead us to trust Jesus fully.
